text:
anna: Rolling up results from the small int8 onboarding (sparrow-mini-int8) canary. Were seeing ~10/1k structured-toolcall failures during multibatch runs. Failures are either top-level arrays or truncated JSON (EOF inside the object). Thoughts?

rob: Do we have raw token streams for a few fails? That will tell us if it's genuine truncation or a postproc mapping bug.

anna: Pasted two sanitized failures below (redacted ids):
```json
// fail A - top-level array returned
[
  {"tool":"send_email","params":{"to":"eng@redwood.ai","subject":"CI"}}
]

// fail B - truncated at end
{"actions": [
  {"tool":"update_ticket","params":{"id":1234,"status":"done"}},
  {"tool":"close_incident","params":{}}
 // EOF here - missing closing brackets
```

kevin: Baseline fp16/float32 runs show no such failures. This started coincident with enabling kvwrap/prefix caching + fast-kernel selection on sequences >400. Batches >=5 increase rate.

ops-bot: canary job 2026-05-12T11:05:00Z started (cj-1122): model=sparrow-mini-int8, nodes=2, batch=8. Capture enabled: raw_tokens + assembler_trace. Logs: https://ci.internal/canary/cj-1122 :mag:

rob: Hypotheses: (1) streaming assembler has a boundary join bug when prefix chunks are hot-swapped from cache, (2) int8 tokenization emits an extra delimiter token early that confuses our JSON normalizer, or (3) a kernel path changes tokenization offsets causing off-by-one in buffer lengths.

kevin: Quick experiments I propose: A) rerun same seed set with kvwrap disabled, B) rerun with a forced terminal sentinel appended to the prompt (e.g., <ACTIONS_END>), C) add a micro-lint in postproc that rejects non-object root shapes and triggers a tiny backoff retry (max 2). If A drops fails significantly that's a strong kvwrap signal.

anna: I already ran A/B on a small sample: kvwrap=off => 0.8/1000 fail; kvwrap=on => 9.7/1000. Anchored prompts with sentinel => 0.4/1000. So looks strongly tied to kvwrap.

bench-bot: quick summary from replay harness (n=5000): kvwrap ON batch=8 seq>400 => 11.2/1000; kvwrap OFF same config => 0.9/1000. Token tail-eof correlation: 72% of fails end exactly at buffer refill boundary.

rob: Buffer refill boundary correlation suggests assembler joining is suspect. Kevin, can you grab assembler_trace around the failing offsets and the kernel selection log? If the assembler applies a memcpy that uses stale length, we could lose the tail bytes.

kevin: grabbing now. If assembler is buggy we should patch to enforce atomic chunk append and validate final byte equals "}" or "]" for JSON before handing to postproc. We'll also push the sentinel injection in retriever as quick mitigation.

anna: For immediate customer impact mitigation I'm going to: 1) enable postproc safe-wrap (arrays -> {"actions": <array>}) as an emergency fallback with a metric tag, 2) enable retry policy linear-2 on the function runner for canary cluster, 3) disable kvwrap for int8 canaries until we have a fix.

rob: Sounds good. Also add a telemetry counter for "assembler_boundary_trim" when payload ends not with a JSON-terminator. That will help gauge residual risk.

ops-bot: canary job cj-1122 logs updated: assembler_trace uploaded, token hex dumps available at https://ci.internal/canary/cj-1122/artifacts :wrench:

kevin: Found suspicious memcpy in stream_assembler.cc: join_chunks(dst, src, len) where len comes from cached_chunk.len but we overwrite dst_len earlier for the first partial chunk. Sending a minimal PR to enforce recompute of total_len after all chunks appended and to assert final byte.

anna: Nice catch. After PR lands we'll re-enable kvwrap on a narrow canary and replay failing seeds. Keep this thread updated with results. If anyone sees a non-retryable malformed output paste raw capture here. :thumbsup:
